nodes.summary: If the four initial curvatures are integers then every curvature of the Apollonian packing they generate is an integer. For example, the packing generated by $(-1, 2, 2, 3)$, a bounding circle of radius $1$ with circles of radii $\tfrac12, \tfrac12, \tfrac13$ inside it, contains the curvatures $15$ (flip the bounding circle) and $35$ (flip the last circle of $(15, 2, 2, 3)$); the tests check both and the strip…
nodes.title: Integral Apollonian packings

nodes.summary: All entries of all quadruples in the Apollonian orbit of `v`; when `v` is the curvature quadruple of a Descartes configuration these are the curvatures of the circles of the packing it generates (H. Oh, arXiv:1312.1383v2, Section 4; Kontorovich and Oh, arXiv:0811.2236v5, Theorem 2.3).
nodes.title: Curvatures of the Apollonian packing of a quadruple

nodes.summary: `Sᵢ² = 1` (Kontorovich and Oh, arXiv:0811.2236v5, introduction: the matrices `Sᵢ` are reflections).
nodes.title: Each Apollonian flip is an involution

nodes.summary: Let $B(u, w) = 2\sum_j u_j w_j - (\sum_j u_j)(\sum_j w_j)$ be the polar form of the Descartes form, so that $B(v, v) = Q(v)$, and let $e_i$ be the $i$-th standard basis vector, which has $Q(e_i) = 1$. Then the orthogonal reflection of the quadratic space $(R^4, Q)$ in the hyperplane $Q$-orthogonal to $e_i$; in Lean it is Mathlib's `Module.reflection` for the linear form $f = 2B(\cdot, e_i)$, which satisfies…
nodes.title: The Apollonian flips are orthogonal reflections

nodes.summary: If $w$ is in the Apollonian orbit of $v$, then so is $S_i w$ for every $i$: append the flip $S_i$ to a word of flips that produces $w$ from $v$.
nodes.title: Apollonian orbits are closed under the flips

nodes.summary: If `B(v, eᵢ) = 0` then `Sᵢ v = v`: `Sᵢ` fixes pointwise the hyperplane `Q`-orthogonal to `eᵢ`.
nodes.title: The Apollonian flips fix the orthogonal hyperplane

nodes.summary: `Sᵢ eᵢ = -eᵢ`; together with the previous statement this identifies `Sᵢ` as the orthogonal reflection of `(R⁴, Q)` along `eᵢ`.
nodes.title: The Apollonian flips negate the reflected vector

nodes.summary: For $i \in \{1, 2, 3, 4\}$, the flip $S_i$ replaces the $i$-th entry of a quadruple by twice the sum of the other three entries minus itself: On the curvatures of a Descartes configuration, $S_i$ replaces the $i$-th circle by the other circle tangent to the remaining three. $S_i$ is multiplication by the matrix that agrees with the identity except in row $i$, which is $(2, 2, 2, 2)$ with $-1$ in position $i$; these…
nodes.title: Apollonian flip

nodes.summary: The quadruples obtained from `v` by finitely many flips; since every flip is an involution this is the orbit of `v` under the Apollonian group `⟨S₁, S₂, S₃, S₄⟩` (Kontorovich and Oh, arXiv:0811.2236v5, Section 2.1).
nodes.title: Apollonian orbit of a quadruple

nodes.summary: `Q(Sᵢ v) = Q(v)`, so the Apollonian group lies in the orthogonal group of `Q` (Kontorovich and Oh, arXiv:0811.2236v5, Section 2.1: `A < O_Q(ℤ)`).
nodes.title: The Apollonian flips preserve the Descartes form

nodes.summary: A quadruple satisfies the Descartes relation `(∑ vᵢ)² = 2 ∑ vᵢ²` exactly when the Descartes quadratic form vanishes on it (Lagarias, Mallows and Wilks, arXiv:math/0101066v1, equation (1.1)).
nodes.title: Descartes relation as a vanishing quadratic form

nodes.summary: Under the hypotheses of Descartes' circle theorem (four circles of positive radii, either pairwise externally tangent or with one circle internally tangent to the three others, which are pairwise externally tangent), the signed curvatures `k` satisfy `Q(k) = 0` (Lagarias, Mallows and Wilks, arXiv:math/0101066v1, Theorem 1.1).
nodes.title: Curvatures of tangent circles form a Descartes quadruple

nodes.summary: Every quadruple in the Apollonian orbit of `v` has the same Descartes form as `v`; in particular the orbit of a Descartes quadruple consists of Descartes quadruples, which lie on the cone `Q = 0` (Kontorovich and Oh, arXiv:0811.2236v5, Section 2.1).
nodes.title: Apollonian orbits stay on a level set of the Descartes form

nodes.summary: `Q(eᵢ) = 2 - 1 = 1`, so each `eᵢ` is anisotropic and has an orthogonal reflection `v ↦ v - 2 B(v, eᵢ) eᵢ`, defined over any commutative ring.
nodes.title: The standard basis vectors have Descartes norm one

nodes.summary: For a quadruple $v = (v_1, v_2, v_3, v_4)$ over a commutative ring, the Descartes quadratic form is A quadruple with $Q(v) = 0$ is a Descartes quadruple. Over $\mathbb{R}$ the form has signature $(3, 1)$, so the Descartes quadruples form a light cone. By Descartes' circle theorem the signed curvatures of four mutually tangent circles form a Descartes quadruple; Kontorovich and Oh use the form with an extra factor…
nodes.title: Descartes quadratic form

nodes.summary: `B(v, v) = Q(v)`, by expanding both sides.
nodes.title: The polar form restricts to the Descartes form on the diagonal

nodes.summary: `B(u, w) = 2 ∑ uᵢ wᵢ - (∑ uᵢ)(∑ wᵢ)`, the symmetric bilinear form with `B(v, v) = Q(v)`. The orthogonal group `O_Q` of Kontorovich and Oh (arXiv:0811.2236v5, Section 2.1) is the group of linear maps preserving it.
nodes.title: Polar form of the Descartes form

nodes.summary: Over an integral domain, let $v$ be a Descartes quadruple and suppose that replacing its $i$-th entry by $x$ again gives a Descartes quadruple. Then $x = v_i$ or $x = 2\sum_{j \ne i} v_j - v_i$.
nodes.title: The two roots of the Descartes relation

nodes.summary: `f(v) = 2 B(v, eᵢ)`, by expanding both sides.
nodes.title: Value of the reflection form

nodes.summary: `f(eᵢ) = 2 Q(eᵢ) = 2`, the normalisation required by `Module.reflection`.
nodes.title: The reflection form is `2` on the reflected vector

nodes.summary: The linear form `f(v) = 4 vᵢ - 2 ∑ vⱼ`, equal to `2 B(v, eᵢ)`; it takes the value `2` on `eᵢ`, so `v ↦ v - f(v) eᵢ` is a reflection in the sense of `Module.reflection`.
nodes.title: The linear form defining the `i`-th Apollonian reflection

nodes.summary: If `v` is integral then so is `Sᵢ v`, because `Sᵢ` has integer entries (Kontorovich and Oh, arXiv:0811.2236v5, equation (1.3) and the remark after it).
nodes.title: Flips preserve integrality

nodes.summary: Every entry of `v` is (the image of) an integer; an Apollonian packing is integral when all its curvatures are (H. Oh, arXiv:1312.1383v2, Section 4).
nodes.title: Integral quadruple

nodes.summary: If the four entries of $v$ are integers, then so are the entries of every quadruple in the Apollonian orbit of $v$: each flip $S_i$ has integer matrix entries.
nodes.title: Integrality propagates through Apollonian orbits

nodes.summary: Every quadruple belongs to its own Apollonian orbit: it is obtained from itself by the empty word of flips.
nodes.title: A quadruple belongs to its Apollonian orbit
